transcript.text: Just got a new Siemens dishwasher and there's always a bit of water left in the bottom under the filter after it finishes. Is it draining properly?

Yes, it is draining properly because if it weren't, the water wouldn't clear at all during the cycle. A small amount of clean water sitting just under the filter is actually normal behaviour to keep the seals wet and prevent odours. However, since you mentioned there is "always" some left, we should rule out a partial blockage which is common in new installs. Please switch off and unplug the machine, then remove the lower rack and twist out the round filter to check if the sump underneath is clear of food or debris.
[Helpful to see: image "Where the filter is" — The filter sits in the base of the dishwasher, usually under the bottom spray arm. Twist it out anticlockwise and rinse it under a tap. Typical layout — your dishwasher may differ.]

Thanks, I've taken the filter out and it's clean, no food or debris. There's just a cupful or so of clean water sitting in the sump under it, and none in the main tub. The hose is looped up under the sink with no kinks. Should I be worried?

No, you don't need to worry because a small amount of clean water in the sump is normal for keeping the seals lubricated and preventing smells. Since your filter is already clean and the hose looks fine, this suggests there might be a specific component causing the retention rather than a blockage. To help me identify that part, could you please check the model number on the side edge of the door? You can send it over whenever you have a moment to look at it.
[Panel: "To check a suitable replacement — Enter your model number below. Once we have the model I can check whether a suitable replacement is available. It's usually on a sticker inside the door or around the frame, or on the back of the appliance."]
The model number is SN23HI60AG. Is there anything else you need from me?

No, I don't need anything else from you right now. Since your filter is clean and the hose looks fine, we can rule out the most common blockages for this model. The next step is to check if something has fallen into the pump area, as a small item like glass or a stone can get stuck there even if it doesn't show up in the main sump. Please switch off and unplug the dishwasher, then look at the small plastic cover near the bottom of the tub where the filter was; lift its clip to see if you can spot anything caught under the impeller.

Okay, I'm a bit wary of taking the pump cover apart on a machine that's only 2 weeks old, in case it affects the warranty. Is that really necessary? The dishwasher is cleaning and drying fine and there are no error codes.

It isn't strictly necessary for the warranty because you are only lifting a small plastic cover with your fingers—no tools or screwdrivers are involved, so it won’t void anything. Since the filter is clean and the hose looks fine, we need to check if something like a stone or piece of glass has fallen into the pump area. Please switch off and unplug the machine, then lift that small pump cover clip to see if you can spot any debris caught under the impeller.

Thanks, that's reassuring about the warranty. Just to be sure though, since it's only a cupful of clean water and everything else works fine, is it definitely worth opening the pump cover? Or is this likely normal for a new machine?

It is most likely worth opening the pump cover because while a small amount of water is normal, it should only be enough to keep the seals wet, not sit as a cupful in the sump. The most common cause for this specific symptom on your model is a small object like a stone or glass shard caught under the impeller, which prevents the last bit of water from draining. Please switch off and unplug the dishwasher, then lift that small plastic cover clip to see if you can spot any debris caught under the impeller.
Okay, that makes sense, I'll have a go. I've switched it off and unplugged it. Where exactly is the pump cover, and how do I lift the clip?

The pump cover is the small rectangular plastic piece located at the very bottom of the sump where you removed the round filter. You can lift its clip by gently prying it upwards with your fingernail or a flat object like a butter knife, then pulling the cover straight up to expose the impeller underneath. Once you have that clear, please check if there is any debris caught under the impeller and let me know what you find.
Thanks. I've got the filter out and lifted the cover, and I can't see any debris, stones or glass under it. What should I do next?

Since you have checked the filter and the pump area without finding any debris, we can move on to checking the drain hose connection at the sink waste. This is a very common issue with brand-new installations because the little blanking plug inside the spigot often needs to be removed for water to flow through properly. Please look under your sink where the grey dishwasher hose joins the waste pipe and check if that small plastic plug is still in place or if it has been cut out.

Thanks. The hose is looped up under the sink with no kinks, but I'm not sure what the blanking plug looks like or whether it's been removed. How would I tell, and is it safe to check with the machine unplugged?

It is perfectly safe to check with the machine unplugged, and you can tell if the plug is in place by looking down into the white plastic spigot on your sink waste where the grey hose connects. If a small circular rubber or plastic disc is blocking the hole inside that spigot, it means the blanking plug hasn't been removed yet. Please check under your sink to see if you can spot this plug and let me know what you find.
